result:
The docstrings and the code disagreed in 9 rules, and I fixed all of them. After the fix I ran a checker that computes the expected price from each docstring. It compared all 150 rules over a grid of qty and unit values, and every rule matched.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 35 | Used `qty > 20`, so 20 units got no discount | `qty >= 20` |
| 109 | Threshold was 13 | Changed to 12 |
| 140 | Threshold was 101 | Changed to 100 |
| 65 | The cap was applied to the amount before the percentage was taken | Compute the discount first, then cap it |
| 69 | Same cap-order mistake as 65 | Same fix |
| 82 | Same cap-order mistake as 65 | Same fix |
| 107 | Should be a "whole" rule but discounted only units above the threshold | Discount based on the full `base` amount |
| 148 | Same as 107 | Same fix |
| 138 | The cap applied only when the discount was over 60,000, so discounts between 30,000 and 60,000 weren't capped | Cap applied always |

Rules 56, 143 and 149 use thresholds that look different from their docstrings (`>= 31`, `> 30`, `> 20`). They are "marginal" rules, so the discount at the threshold quantity is 0 either way, and the result is the same. I left them as they were.

STATUS: DONE
